cards.text: The LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, has a word about Moab, the nation that came from Lot's son Moab (Genesis 19:37). And friend, it does NOT open with "Hope you're doing well." It opens with woe to Nebo, a town in Moab, because it will be devastated.

cards.question: Next on the list is Kiriathaim, another town in Moab. The LORD says it will be captured and disgraced.

cards.text: And the praise Moab used to get? Gone. Over in Heshbon, people are plotting evil against her.

cards.question: The people in Heshbon are plotting evil against Moab. What do they say they'll do to her?

cards.text: Then the LORD turns to a town called Madmen. Friend, I didn't name it. I'm just reading it.

cards.question: The LORD says the people of Madmen will be silenced, and the ___ will pursue them.

cards.text: A voice cries out from Horonaim: "Devastation and great destruction!" Then it gets heavy, friend: Moab will be shattered, and her little ones will cry out.

cards.question: Moab's people are on the road, going up the ascent to Luhith. What are they doing as they go?
The cries of distress on the descent to Horonaim tell Moab to stand and fight.

cards.text: Nope. The cry is "Flee! Run for your lives! Become like a juniper in the desert." Then the LORD says why Moab will be captured.

cards.question: Why does the LORD say Moab will be captured?

answers.text: Moab trusts in its works and treasures
Moab mocks the prophets of the LORD
Moab bows down to the sun and stars

cards.question: It's not just the people. Chemosh, the god of the Moabites (1 Kings 11:33), will go into ___ with his priests and officials.
The LORD says a few of Moab's towns will escape the destroyer.
The LORD says to put salt on Moab. What will her cities become?

answers.text: Desolate with no one living in them
Crowded with people running from war
Fortresses for the destroyer to keep

cards.text: Now friend, slow down for this next one, because it's a hard line: cursed is the one who is remiss in doing the work of the LORD.

cards.question: In that hard line about the work of the LORD, who else is called cursed?

answers.text: The one who holds back his sword from bloodshed
The one who takes the treasures of Moab
The one who mourns for the towns of Moab

cards.text: Now the LORD paints a picture: Moab has been at ease from youth, settled like wine on its dregs, never poured from vessel to vessel or gone into exile. Friend, I spent YEARS in the back of a junk drawer, and even I got shoved around more than that.

cards.question: Moab is like wine that never gets poured from vessel to vessel. What does the LORD say about his flavor and aroma?
The LORD says the days are coming when He will send wanderers to Moab. What will they do to him?

answers.text: Pour him out and shatter his jars
Carry his jars off as plunder
Tear down the walls around him

cards.question: Once Moab is poured out like that, who will Moab be ashamed of?

cards.text: And the LORD doesn't stop there, friend. He holds up Israel as the comparison: "just as the house of Israel was ashamed when they trusted in Bethel."

Then comes a question: "How can you say, 'We are warriors, mighty men ready for battle'?" That's the same energy as me promising a baker I can carry TWELVE cookie boxes with one mustache, and friend, I have DROPPED two.

cards.question: The King, whose name is the LORD of Hosts, says the best of Moab's young men will win the battle.
How soon does the LORD say Moab's calamity will come?

answers.text: It is at hand and rushing swiftly
It will come after many generations
It will come in his grandsons' days

cards.text: Now the LORD turns to the neighbors: all who surround Moab, everyone who knows his name. Picture every neighbor on the street leaning out the window at the same time.

cards.question: The LORD tells everyone around Moab to celebrate his fall.

cards.text: Not even close, they're told to MOURN for him and tell how the mighty scepter is shattered. And the daughter dwelling in Dibon has to come down from her glory and sit on parched ground, which is a LONG way down, friend.

cards.question: Why is the daughter dwelling in Dibon told to come down from her glory?

answers.text: The destroyer of Moab has come against her
She has turned away from the LORD her God
Her king has been taken away as a captive

cards.text: Whoever lives in Aroer is told to stand by the road and watch, and ask the man fleeing or the woman escaping, "What has happened?" That's you stopping a coworker sprinting out of the building like, "Wait, WAIT, what happened?"

cards.question: Then comes a word about Moab. It is put to shame, because it has been ___.

cards.text: Then comes the cry: "Wail and cry out! Declare by the Arnon that Moab is destroyed." No soft landing on this one, friend.

Then judgment comes on the high plain, town after town: Holon, Jahzah, Mephaath, Dibon and more, all the towns of Moab, far and near. And look who's back on the list, friend: Nebo and Kiriathaim, the first two towns named at the very start.

cards.question: The LORD closes by saying Moab's arm is still strong.

cards.text: The horn of Moab has been cut off and his arm is broken, declares the LORD. That's where we'll leave Moab for now, friend, because the LORD's word about him isn't finished.

findings.problem: The blank asks for the unseen wording of the prophetic line. Earlier cards do not give the baker a way to reason out "sword" rather than "wind" or "plague," so this is a wording guess rather than a test of meaning.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The blank asks for the next word of a line the baker has not seen. Being told that Moab will be captured does not establish whether Chemosh goes into exile, battle or hiding, so the baker is left guessing.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: "In that hard line" and "who else" depend on story card 15, which is no longer on screen. The question needs to restate the first curse so that it stands on its own.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: Discovery questions dominate the stop. Cards 2, 4, 9, 11 and 13, along with the fill-in-the-blank problems on cards 6 and 12, ask for unrevealed details that cannot be reasoned out from the earlier cards. This goes beyond the allowed few discovery questions.

rule.text:
Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer.

A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

findings.problem: Story cards 3 and 5 each have three sentences. Card 10 also has three narrator sentences even when its whole quotation is treated as one unit. Only the opening story card may run to three sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.
